newsitem.title: UK: Iraq sugar freight orders emerge but market thin.
newsitem.headline: Iraq sugar freight orders emerge but market thin.

text.p: Iraq was the feature of the day on an otherwise quiet sugar freight market as two inquiries emerged for bagged cargoes leaving from north and south Brazil, shipbrokers said on Monday. Czarnikow Rionda was looking to cover 14,000 tonnes in bags from south Brazil to Aqaba or Iraq's Gulf port of Umm Qasr for 1/10 January and Genoc quoted for a same-sized cargo from north Brazil to Mediterrean, Red Sea, Umm Qasr, Pakistan or Colombo.
Dates were prompt/five days notice. Genoc also quoted for 32/33,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Salaverry to US Gulf/Atlantic for prompt/5 January shipment.

It was also in the market for 11/12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar, and up to 14,000, from Buenaventura to Sri Lanka/east Africa with options including Madagascar, Red Sea, Pakisan, Bangladesh and Indonesia. Czarnikow Rionda was open with other inquiry, quoting for 16/25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from the Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic for 15/30 January and 12/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from east coast Mexico to Mediterranean/west Africa for 1/10 January.
Louis Dreyfus issued an inquiry for 14,300 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to Indonesia for 10/15 January.
Iran again featured as a sugar destination, with Seabon open on account for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from the Netherlands to Iran for prompt onwards dates.
Elsewhere, an Turkish industry ministry official said Turkey had agreed with Iran to sell it 50,000 tonnes of sugar from its stocks and more sugar exports might come later.
